candidate.title: X-ChIP
candidate.scope: The assigned X-ChIP middle row, resolved as the depicted MNase-based high-resolution crosslinking implementation and called X-ChIP-seq by the matching secondary catalogue. This does not prescribe all X-ChIP protocols. The complete route is cell → in-vivo crosslinked cell → lysed cross-linked chromatin → MNase digestion → sonication/soluble extract → combined immunoprecipitation and DNA extraction → DNA. The yellow-highlighted chromatin at left illustrates the mapping concept and has no material-transfer arrow to the starting cell. Orange marks accompany the MNase caption and an antibody-like icon accompanies immunoprecipitation; no specific target identity or DNA end chemistry is shown. PAT-ChIP above, ORGANIC below and the top-edge cropped FiT-Seq captions are independently named neighboring rows, without branches grouping them into X-ChIP. The diagram ends at DNA; library preparation and sequencing are supported downstream interfaces, not depicted operations.

X-ChIP-seq denotes its sequencing readout here, not a second depicted alternative. Scope revision removes previous PAT-ChIP, ORGANIC and FiT-Seq assignments, their separate material graphs and the resulting out-of-scope unknowns: independently labelled neighbors have no branching arrows that group them into X-ChIP. No neighboring material is redirected into this route. The retained input histories preserve fixation before lysis, digestion and sonication; shared operation labels do not establish equivalence with native or FFPE preparations.
